Concept.description: One entity a guide answer may refer to: an authority, a permit, a step in a process, a document, a legal status, a service, a legal act, or a term of art. Closed world - an entity absent from the register cannot be asserted.

alt_labels.description: Other surface forms the same entity is published under, including abbreviations and superseded names. They are how a reader, and a model asked to name the entity, recognise it under more than one name.

broader.description: The more general concept this one falls under.

change_note.description: What changed, in one sentence, when this entity was superseded or re-scoped.

close_match.description: An external concept close enough to be useful but not equivalent. Used where YSO carries the general term and the register carries the Finnish administrative specific.

definition.description: A short gloss, in whichever languages have been reviewed.

exact_match.description: An external concept this one is equivalent to, in YSO, JUPO, PTV, or another published vocabulary.

handled_by.description: The authority responsible for this permit, step, or service. Time-sliced by the validity of both ends, which is what makes "who was responsible in year N" answerable.

id.description: Stable IRI, written as a CURIE whose prefix matches ``kind`` (``org:`` for an organization, ``permit:`` for a permit, and so on).

in_scope_of.description: The guides whose remit this concept falls within. A guide's scope is the set of concepts naming it here, which is what gate G3 checks instead of a hand-written English sentence.

kind.description: What sort of entity this is. Determines the IRI prefix and the RDF type.

notation.description: The code this entity carries in an official code list, where it has one.

observations.description: Where this entity was seen, and when. At least one per concept: the register records what a named source said on a given date, and this is what lets a reader judge its coverage rather than take it on faith.

pref_label.description: The one preferred label per language. Every concept carries all three.

related.description: An associative link that is not subsumption.

superseded_by.description: What took this entity's place. Populated whenever ``valid_until`` is set, and what lets G5 auto-repair a stale assertion without a second model call.

valid_from.description: The earliest date from which the register is prepared to treat this entity as in force. Where a source names a commencement date, that date is used; otherwise it is the register's floor date, which records that the register has no evidence of a start date and asserts nothing earlier. Required from day one: it is what lets gate G5 check a historical claim against the state of affairs at its own reference date rather than against today.

valid_until.description: The last date on which this entity was in force, inclusive, and absent while it still is. A body dissolved on 1 January 2025 therefore carries 2024-12-31, and its successor's ``valid_from`` is 2025-01-01, so the two intervals meet without a gap or an overlap. A present-tense claim naming a concept whose ``valid_until`` has passed fails G5.

ConceptKind.description: The sort of entity a concept denotes, and the IRI prefix it takes.
ConceptKind.title: ConceptKind

Definitions.description: A short gloss, per language. Languages are filled in as they are reviewed.
Definitions.title: Definitions

GuideId.description: The guides in the network, per ADR 0005.
GuideId.title: GuideId

Observation.description: One record of a source stating something about a concept, on a date.

note.description: What this source contributed, where that is not obvious.

observed_on.description: When Tapio looked, which is not when reality changed. The distinction matters when reading the register as a record of administrative change.

source.description: The publisher the observation came from.

url.description: The exact page or API response observed, not a site root.

Observation.title: Observation

PrefLabels.description: The preferred label in each of the three languages the corpus is grounded in. The pattern rejects an empty or whitespace-only label, which ``required`` alone permits and which would publish a concept with no name to render or resolve against.
PrefLabels.title: PrefLabels

SourceId.description: The publishers the register is seeded from, per the ontological harness specification section 10.
SourceId.title: SourceId

TermRegister.description: One dated, immutable edition of the register. Concepts are never removed between editions: an entity that leaves force gains a ``valid_until`` and a ``superseded_by`` pointer instead (ADR 0007, decision 5).

coverage_caveat.description: The statement of what the register does and does not record, published with every edition. The register records what its sources said on the dates they were observed, not ground truth; a gap in it is evidence of a gap in Tapio's attention, not evidence that nothing happened.

description.description: What this edition covers, in one paragraph.

license.description: SPDX-style identifier or URL of the licence the edition is released under.

register_version.description: The release date of this edition, used verbatim as the ``register_version`` field of a provenance record. Dated and immutable, never a rolling identifier such as "main".
